input:
The staffing ramp for the upgrade project has been set at 9%, and this figure has been retained against the lower alternative put to the steering group. A ramp of this kind is not a contingency allowance by another name. The cost table set out in the Costs section prices the posts that the project needs, and the ramp determines the rate at which those posts are filled. The lower alternative, it should be noted, fills exactly the same posts, only more slowly, and the saving it appears to offer is a saving in the early periods only, since the establishment itself is unchanged.

The case for holding the ramp at 9% rests on sequencing. Where posts are filled late, they arrive after the work they support has started, and the programme then has to carry the gap, either as delay or as bought-in cover, neither of which is visible in the comparison the lower alternative invites. Where posts are filled at the ramp rate, by contrast, they arrive in the order in which the work packages need them. The steering group is therefore not being asked to fund a larger establishment, but rather to fund the establishment in the cost table at the rate at which the programme actually consumes it, and a lower ramp would simply move cost out of the early periods and into delay, where it becomes harder to see and harder to recover.
